executiveSummary: Surveillance data from ECDC and PAHO covering late 2025 through May 2026 reveals multiple concurrent biological threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) continues to circulate in the Americas with ongoing animal-to-human spillover risk, representing a critical pandemic preparedness concern. Mpox transmission persists in the Americas region alongside elevated dengue, chikungunya, and yellow fever activity. Additional threats include rising pertussis cases, measles resurgence, and the start of the Southern Hemisphere influenza season signaling increased respiratory virus burden.
bottomLine: Multiple concurrent infectious disease threats—led by H5N1 avian influenza spillover risk, mpox, and vector-borne disease surges—demand heightened surveillance and coordinated response across the Americas and Europe.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating ongoing circulation
Continued animal reservoir activity with human spillover risk
Select agent with pandemic potential requiring BSL-3 containment protocols
threats.action: Strengthen zoonotic surveillance at animal-human interface, enforce PPE protocols for exposed workers, accelerate H5N1 vaccine candidate stockpiling, and activate rapid response protocols for any confirmed human case clusters

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 23, 2026 confirming ongoing transmission
Sustained community spread in multiple Americas countries
BSL-3 select agent with potential for international spread
threats.action: Enhance case detection and contact tracing, expand JYNNEOS vaccination coverage for high-risk populations, reinforce cross-border notification protocols, and maintain BSL-3 laboratory capacity for confirmatory diagnostics

threats.name: Dengue Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological update February 2026 indicating elevated case counts
Historically high dengue burden entering peak transmission season
Concurrent circulation with chikungunya increasing diagnostic and clinical complexity
threats.action: Intensify vector control operations, enhance hospital surge capacity for severe dengue, accelerate dengue early warning systems, and coordinate cross-border entomological surveillance

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 13, 2026
Epizootic activity in non-human primates signaling active viral circulation
Risk of urban transmission in under-vaccinated populations
threats.action: Reinforce vaccination campaigns in at-risk areas, strengthen epizootic surveillance as early warning indicator, ensure adequate yellow fever vaccine stockpiles, and enforce vaccination requirements for international travelers

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two consecutive PAHO alerts issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained rise
Resurgence pattern consistent with waning vaccine immunity and potential pathogen evolution
High-risk impact on infants and immunocompromised populations
threats.action: Review and strengthen routine childhood immunization coverage, implement Tdap boosters for pregnant women and healthcare workers, investigate potential vaccine escape variants through whole-genome sequencing

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 3, 2026
Circulation in region previously certified as measles-eliminated
Pandemic-era vaccination gaps creating susceptible birth cohorts
threats.action: Conduct urgent supplementary immunization activities targeting under-vaccinated communities, investigate importation chains, strengthen measles-rubella surveillance, and ensure outbreak response capacity at national and subnational levels

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 10, 2026
Co-circulation with dengue complicating clinical diagnosis and case management
Expanding Aedes mosquito habitat range increasing transmission risk
threats.action: Enhance integrated vector management, train clinicians on differential diagnosis from dengue, strengthen laboratory confirmation capacity, and monitor for neurological complications in vulnerable populations

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza and RSV
signals: PAHO alert January 2026 on simultaneous influenza and RSV circulation
PAHO April 2026 alert marking start of Southern Hemisphere 2026 influenza season
Dual pathogen burden straining healthcare systems with overlapping respiratory illness presentations
threats.action: Promote seasonal influenza vaccination uptake, monitor RSV hospitalizations in elderly and pediatric populations, ensure antiviral stockpiles and healthcare surge capacity, and conduct real-time genomic surveillance for novel influenza variants

selectAgentSummary: Two BSL-3/BSL-4 relevant pathogens detected in this surveillance cycle: (1) Avian Influenza A(H5N1) — a Tier 1 select agent with demonstrated pandemic potential — continues to circulate in animal reservoirs across the Americas with ongoing human spillover risk, flagged as Critical threat level. (2) Monkeypox virus (MPXV) — a BSL-3 select agent — remains in active community transmission across the Americas as of April 2026, flagged as Elevated threat level. Both require strict biosafety protocols, enhanced laboratory containment, and international reporting under IHR 2005 frameworks.

amrSignals: Bordetella pertussis population genomics should be monitored for macrolide resistance emergence given sustained resurgence despite high vaccination coverage
Influenza antiviral resistance surveillance warranted as H5N1 and seasonal strains co-circulate — oseltamivir resistance mutations require active monitoring
Dengue and arboviral co-circulation may complicate empiric antibiotic use decisions, indirectly driving AMR through misdiagnosis-driven prescribing
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous multi-pathogen surge in the Americas suggesting systemic surveillance and healthcare system stress across the region
Post-pandemic immunization gap driving resurgence of vaccine-preventable diseases including measles and pertussis in previously controlled settings
Expanding arboviral burden (dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever) coinciding with climate-driven Aedes range expansion across the Americas
H5N1 continued enzootic spread in Americas animal populations with multiple PAHO updates over four months indicating failure to contain at animal reservoir level
Start of Southern Hemisphere influenza season coinciding with active RSV circulation creating compounded respiratory disease burden
GLP-1 receptor agonist medication misuse flagged as emerging public health concern in Americas, indicating expansion of surveillance scope to include pharmaceutical safety signals
